text.en: Believing superheavy elements become progressively less stable in a smooth, monotonic way as atomic number increases, with no possibility of a heavier element being unexpectedly more stable than its lighter neighbours -- the nuclear shell model predicts that closed proton and neutron shells produce local peaks of extra stability regardless of overall mass, the same effect responsible for ordinary 'magic number' nuclei being more tightly bound than their neighbours, so certain specific superheavy proton and neutron numbers are predicted to produce a genuinely more stable 'island' rather than a continuously worsening trend.
text.et: Arvamus, et üliraske elemendid muutuvad progressiivselt vähem stabiilseks sujuval, monotoonsel viisil, kui aatomnumber kasvab, ilma võimaluseta, et raskem element oleks ootamatult stabiilsem kui selle kergemad naabrid -- tuuma kihimudel ennustab, et kinnised prooton- ja neutronikihid tekitavad kohalikke lisastabiilsuse tippe olenemata kogumassist, sama efekt, mis vastutab selle eest, et tavalised 'maagilise arvuga' tuumad on nende naabritest tugevamini seotud, seega ennustatakse, et teatud konkreetsed üliraskete elementide prootonite ja neutronite arvud tekitavad tõeliselt stabiilsema 'saare', mitte pidevalt halveneva trendi.
